findings.description: F005 allows gitignored files to be deleted with an otherwise clean worktree, but the objective contract says cleanup only happens when clean and dirty or untracked files are never deleted automatically. Unless ignored files are explicitly excluded from the contract's meaning of untracked, this creates a user-facing cleanup semantics mismatch.
findings.recommendation: Either make ignored files block removal, or amend the objective and tests to explicitly define ignored files as regenerable non-blocking state for v0 cleanup.

findings.description: F003 requires override-with-reason recording and F002 requires binding snapshot capture, but the proposed acceptance does not pin failure behavior if those evidence writes fail before the guarded command performs its side effects. The operator outcome requires overrides to be recorded, so an override path that proceeds without durable evidence would violate the contract.
findings.recommendation: Specify audit/evidence-first ordering for override execution and add a negative test proving side effects do not run when override evidence or snapshot capture cannot be written.

findings.description: F006 derives the deterministic worktree path from only the repository directory name and plan id, while the registry is install-level and records repo_root. Two repositories or checkouts with the same directory basename and plan id will collide at the filesystem path and block otherwise valid isolated-plan-start flows.
findings.recommendation: Include a stable repo identity component such as a sanitized repo_root hash in the deterministic path, or explicitly pin v0 to a single repo basename namespace.
